html:
Kosala was a powerful kingdom of the 6th and 5th centuries BCE in the plain north of the Ganges, one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas. Its capital was Shravasti, and Ayodhya, or Saketa, was one of its cities.

Kosala was among the first states in India to shift from rule by clans to rule by a king. It swallowed the old kingdom of Kashi and became the main rival of Magadha. Its king Prasenajit was a friend and follower of the Buddha, who spent many rainy seasons at the Jetavana monastery in Shravasti.

Prasenajit's son Vidudabha seized the throne and is said to have destroyed the Shakyas, the Buddha's own clan. Soon after, Magadha under Ajatashatru defeated Kosala and took its lands. Ayodhya later became famous as the city of Rama in the Ramayana.
